title: Program Manager, Enterprise Growth & Capital Programs
jd_text: At Jabil (NYSE: JBL), we are proud to be a trusted partner for the world's top brands, offering comprehensive engineering, supply chain, and manufacturing solutions. With 60 years of experience across industries and a vast network of over 100 sites worldwide, Jabil combines global reach with local expertise to deliver both scalable and customized solutions. Our commitment extends beyond business success as we strive to build sustainable processes that minimize environmental impact and foster vibrant and diverse communities around the globe. Role Overview The Program Manager – is responsible for the end‑to‑end delivery of enterprise‑level growth programs, including new site builds, site expansions, and facilities readiness required to meet committed product launch timelines. This role owns programs from requirements definition through site launch and operational handoff, working backwards from target launch dates to ensure facilities, infrastructure, resources, and cross‑functional capabilities are fully aligned. The Program Manager acts as the single point of accountability and applies Project Management Institute (PMI) standards to ensure disciplined planning, execution, and delivery across multiple complex programs. effectiveness and business impact Design and facilitate training related to enterprise initiatives and program implementation Demonstrate strong customer focus by anticipating needs, resolving issues title: TACOM (RRAD): Computer Systems Analyst II (Contingency)
jd_text: Title: TACOM (RRAD): Computer Systems Analyst II (Contingency) Program Summary The U.S. Army Tank-automotive and Armaments Command (TACOM) sustains the Army’s mission to develop, acquire, field, and sustain ground combat, tactical, and support systems throughout their lifecycle. The program focuses on ensuring operational readiness, reliability, and safety of automotive and ground support equipment critical to Army operations. Under this contract, personnel provide maintenance, repair, overhaul, and sustainment support in accordance with Army technical manuals, safety standards, and performance requirements. Job Summary The Computer Systems Analyst II analyzes, designs, and supports information systems to meet TACOM mission and operational requirements. This role evaluates system performance, identifies improvements, and ensures that hardware, software, and network solutions function effectively and securely. This position works with limited supervision, performs moderately complex system analysis tasks, and may provide guidance to junior personnel. This position is contingent upon award Roles and Responsibilities Proposes and develops automated reports using the Logistics Modernization Program’s Enterprise Data Warehouse (EDW), Enterprise Central Component (ECC), or the Workload Planning and Reporting Module or associated systems to improve data collection, reporting, analysis, and forecasting. Uses model-based software to analyze and prepare reports for analysis. Establishes rapport with production functions to analyze, verify, and correct workload data ensuring data availability of workload factors including parts, production orders, labor hours and timekeeping, schedules, etc. Maintains products and reports between LMP and manual and automated systems which establish, implement, maintain, and evaluate (a.) operating or mission programs of the depot; (b.) pertinent administrative or support programs of the depot; (c.) integration of the programs; and (d.) their interrelationships with the related support functions of the depot. Provides advice on the development, testing, and roll out decisions to depot personnel with input from independent contractors, higher headquarters, and Army guidance. Performs a variety of duties involving various automated supply systems supporting depot organizations and tenant activities. Works independently utilizing skills, knowledge, and abilities such as interview, use of appropriate analytical and investigative management techniques, systems and procedures analyses, forms and reports analysis, work simplifications, statistical analysis, ADP systems analysis, supply systems analysis and similar techniques in the study, development, evaluation, revision, or improvement of depot programs and procedures necessary for efficient and economical accomplishment. Incumbent may be requested to perform any one or all the following functions independently. Conducts studies and audits of depot performance, compliance, and progress toward improvement of objectives and efficiency in a variety of supply management programs. Management studies/audits involve a comprehensive evaluation of managerial and ADP systems functions resulting in a wide impact on depot organizations. Studies may be assigned or conducted on initiative of analysts and require an extensive knowledge of depot mission and supply functions and a thorough knowledge of the uses and potential uses of ADP systems and automation to interface with mission and supply systems accomplishment. Makes judgmental recommendations for changes in work/supply systems, sometimes recommending significant departure from established or regulatory procedures. Detailed study in draft form is submitted to supervisor for review and in final form to concerned management officials/depot commander, with analysis available for discussion, advice, and service upon implementation. Serves as consultant to management and staff elements concerning assigned supply systems and program problems and provide recommendations of solution based on own judgment. Serves as system analyst and advisor/consultant in the installation supply, property accountability, and equipment authorization and transportation management programs, in the design, development, and maintenance of new and existing systems/programs. Analyzes system processing problems and provides technical assistance to functional personnel to alleviate these problems. As assigned, represents the depot at higher command meetings to exchange information and coordinate functional program/system objectives, clarify depot policy and directives, and resolve controversial problems. Coordinate minor and complex design changes to supply systems and functional procedures with associated directorates on depot, with headquarters, and vendors to assure continuity and to enable trouble-free transitions. Serves as depot point of contact for each current assigned program and overall functional and system coordinator for program redesign and development through interface with Directorate of Information Management programmers and external system design agencies. Plans and coordinates statistical reporting and record keeping related to installation supply accounting and management, analyzes to detect deficiencies within the directorate and in supporting divisions, and other depot activities supporting the directorate. Reports findings and develop recommendations for procedural and regulatory changes using own judgment and knowledge of the system and regulations. Develops informative material detailing relating to such factors as organization or responsibility, correlation of activities, including those at higher echelons and control points, interpretation of new or revised regulations, etc. Presents material in written or charted form for dissemination or presents as a contribution for directorate of command presentations and meetings. Analyzes methods of attaining established program objectives and reviewing supply management systems. Develop guidelines and procedures to facilitate accomplishments. Develops training programs and provides instruction. Advises management and functional personnel on system requirements and limitations to systems to assist users in defining problems and needs. This requires a broad knowledge and understanding of logistics systems flow, terminology, and interrelationships with those systems (both local unique and standard) which interface with Army Material Command Installation Supply System (AMCISS), Standard Depot Systems (SDS) and other division Systems. Performs other duties as assigned. Basic Qualifications Education/Experience: High school diploma or GED. Must be computer literate and proficient in Microsoft Excel, Word, and Power Point. Knowledge of a broad range of supply program relationships to monitor automated programs to determine their efficiency in meeting established information requirements and recommend changes in data flow, sources of input, report formats, and calculations to satisfy supply management information needs. Knowledge of specialized methods and techniques to analyze and evaluate the effectiveness and efficiency of supply integrated systems. Ability to analyze and resolve difficult issues and problems in supply data management, i.e., accept requests for system changes, conduct research to determine the validity of requests, refine the information provided, and prepare specifications for computer specialists to use in programming, testing, and implementing changes in automated supply systems in collaboration with computer specialists, they evaluate problems with new and modified systems, including the logical flow, input errors, interconnections among data fields and program elements within a flow of related programs, and recommend solutions to both supply and computer specialists. Skill in analytical reasoning and the ability to apply that skill to the identification, analysis, and resolution of budgetary and workforce utilization problems. Knowledge of analytical and evaluative techniques. Knowledge of budgeting/accounting practices, internal support programs, depot support functions, and automated systems. Skill in applying such techniques to studies concerning the efficiency and effectiveness of operating and administrative programs, including pertinent manual and automated systems. Knowledge of major issues, program goals and objectives, direct labor work processes, and major administrative operations of the depot; their integration; and their interrelationships with the related support functions of the Depot and its tenants. Ability to obtain or maintain a U.S. Government security clearance (as required) U.S. citizenship required Preferred Qualifications Previous experience supporting DoD, Army, or TACOM programs Prior government contracting experience Additional Information This position will be performed in office, data center, or operational environment that requires prolonged sitting, computer use, and occasional movement within facilities. Employees may also be required to work shifts, overtime, or weekend support based on mission needs. KBR Benefits KBR offers a selection of competitive lifestyle benefits which could include 401K plan with company match, medical, dental, vision, life insurance, AD&D, flexible spending account, disability, paid time off, or flexible work schedule. We support career advancement through professional training and development. Belong, Connect and Grow at KBR At KBR, we are passionate about our people and our Zero Harm culture. title: Product Operations and Portfolio Program Manager
location: Spring, Texas, United States of America
jd_text: Product Operations and Portfolio Program Manager Description - HP's Personal Systems business spans PCs, displays, software, and services designed for commercial, consumer, and gaming customers worldwide. At the center of this portfolio is HP's commitment to delivering secure, manageable, and differentiated end-user experiences that scale across global enterprises, governments, and SMBs. As security threats continue to evolve, HP integrates protection across the entire Personal Systems ecosystem, from hardware and firmware to software, cloud services, and security solutions, enabling customers to confidently deploy and manage their fleets without compromising performance, usability, or resilience. HP Wolf Security is a market-leading endpoint security portfolio that combines hardware-enforced security, threat containment, endpoint management, and cloud-based services to protect customers from modern cyber threats. The portfolio spans secure PCs, firmware and BIOS protection, cloud management platforms, endpoint security solutions, and innovative security services. The Product Operations and Portfolio Program Manager provides operational leadership and business management across the HP Security GBU. This is a senior role which establishes the processes, governance, analytics, and cross-functional alignment needed to translate Security GBU strategy into measurable business and product outcomes. Operating across product management, engineering, and teams internal and external to the GBU, this role drives portfolio execution, maintains operational rigor, identifies business and delivery risks, and ensures that decisions result in clear ownership and follow-through. The role serves as a central coordination point for complex initiatives that span organizational boundaries and do not have a single functional owner. Key Responsibiliti es 1. Portfolio Governance and Roadmap Operations Establish and maintain governance processes for the Security GBU product portfolio, including roadmap reviews, prioritization, release tracking, and executive decision support. Coordinate the internal and external roadmap processes across product management, engineering, support, category, sales, and other stakeholders. Consolidate product-manager inputs into an external roadmap appropriate for broader HP audiences, facilitate periodic reviews, and route stakeholder feedback back to product owners. Identify roadmap gaps, delivery risks, missing ownership, dependencies, and items without credible release dates. Drive decisions on whether portfolio items should be completed, re-planned, escalated, removed, or moved to future planning periods. 2. Program Leadership and Operating-Model Improvement Lead complex, cross-functional programs that coordinate product management, engineering, and supporting functions. Provide direction to project leads while maintaining program-level accountability for scope, stakeholder alignment, executive communication, and results. Establish clear divisions of responsibility among program sponsors, program leadership, project managers, product managers, and functional teams. 3. Business Performance, Forecasting, and Executive Analytics Own recurring analysis of Security GBU product, revenue, shipment, attach, activation, licensing, and subscription performance. Develop and maintain consolidated operating dashboards, business-performance files, forecasts, projections, and management views. Create concise executive insights that explain performance, risks, assumptions, and recommended actions. 4. Partner, Supplier, and Contract Coordination Support operational management of strategic technology suppliers and partners when responsibilities span product, finance, legal, procurement, and business leadership. Maintain working knowledge of contractual obligations, royalty structures, licensed components, reporting requirements, and amendment needs. Coordinate the stakeholders required for supplier negotiations, contract changes, payment questions, and new partnership opportunities. 5. Go-to-Market Enablement Help Sales, WW Category, customer-success, and technical teams navigate the Security GBU portfolio, supported platforms, product configurations, and operational processes. Ensure recurring field questions and customer needs are converted into documented requirements, market requests, Jira items, roadmap decisions, or enablement content. Support customer-specific opportunities by validating product availability, configurations, dependencies, and implementation paths. Qualifications and Experience Extensive experience leading complex global programs, portfolio operations, business operations, or product operations in a matrixed technology organization. Demonstrated ability to operate across product management, engineering, finance, category, sales, supply chain, legal, and customer-success functions. Strong understanding of product-development lifecycle, portfolio governance, roadmap management, new-product introduction, and commercial operations. Advanced analytical skills, including business modeling, forecasting, trend analysis, data reconciliation, and executive insight development. Advanced Excel and PowerPoint capabilities, with experience creating management dashboards and decision-oriented presentations. Experience with Jira, SharePoint, Teams, and enterprise ordering, financial, and reporting systems. Strong program structuring, stakeholder management, risk management, written communication, negotiation, and executive-presentation skills. Ability to independently manage multiple complex workstreams with limited oversight. Technical fluency sufficient to work effectively with security-product, software, firmware, hardware, and platform-engineering teams. Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience required; advanced business, technical, or program-management education preferred. Location & working model This position is based in Houston, Texas. Candidates should be located within a commutable distance of the Houston area. This role operates under a hybrid working arrangement, with a minimum requirement to be onsite three days per week. As a people-focused senior role, regular in-person collaboration is encouraged to support stakeholder engagement, team leadership, and business impact. The Houston site provides a collaborative workplace environment with access to meeting and conference facilities, wellness resources, fitness facilities, food services, and a range of onsite employee amenities. The location supports both in-person collaboration and hybrid working arrangements. The pay range for this role is $147,050 to $205,000 USD annually with additional opportunities for pay in the form of bonus and/or equity (applies to United States of America candidates only). Pay varies by work location, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Benefits: HP offers a comprehensive benefits package for this position, including: Health insurance Dental insurance Vision insurance Long term/short term disability insurance Employee assistance program Flexible spending account Life insurance Generous time off policies, including; 4-12 weeks fully paid parental leave based on tenure 11 paid holidays Additional flexible paid vacation and sick leave ( US benefits overview ) The compensation and benefits information is accurate as of the date of this posting. title: Lead Technical Product Manager – Commerce Platform
jd_text: Calling all originals: At Levi Strauss & Co., you can be yourself — and be part of something bigger. We're a company of people who like to forge our own path and leave the world better than we found it. Who believe that what makes us different makes us stronger. So add your voice. Make an impact. Find your fit — and your future. We are looking for an experienced Lead Technical Product Manager to help define the strategy for our global Commerce Platform. The Commerce Platform provides foundational capabilities that power Levi's digital commerce experiences across channels and markets. These capabilities span areas including product and inventory, cart and checkout, payments, promotions, identity, search, analytics, observability, and the services and integrations that connect our broader commerce ecosystem. We are undergoing a significant transformation, evolving from a legacy monolithic commerce platform to a modern architecture built on domain-driven services, APIs, event-driven integration, and reusable platform capabilities. As the Lead Technical Product Manager, you will define the strategy and roadmap for key Commerce Platform capabilities, partnering closely with Engineering, Architecture, Digital Product, and business stakeholders to turn customer and commercial needs into scalable technical solutions. Beyond gathering and prioritizing requirements, you will help shape the platform's future. This includes identifying opportunities for reusable platform capabilities, addressing architectural and process constraints, prioritizing investments that unlock long-term value, and balancing short-term needs against long-term scalability and complexity. You will bring product judgment, technical fluency, and curiosity. You are comfortable operating in a changing landscape, digging into complex systems and business processes, challenging assumptions, and bringing structure and direction to problems that cross technical boundaries. About the Job Technical Product Roadmap • Build and evolve the product strategy for defined capabilities within the Commerce Platform. • Translate customer, business, and commercial needs into scalable technical products and platform capabilities. • Partner with Engineering and Architecture to shape platform strategy, identifying opportunities to unlock value through new technologies and architectural capabilities while proactively addressing technical constraints, tradeoffs, and long-term risks. • Balance near-term needs with foundational platform investments, technical health, scalability, reliability, and long-term maintainability. • Build toward reusable, configurable platform capabilities rather than market-, channel-, or use-case-specific implementations. • Identify opportunities to simplify the platform, reduce duplication, and establish clearer product and domain boundaries. • Define clear product outcomes and success measures and use them to guide roadmap decisions. Product Discovery, Definition & Execution • Lead the end-to-end product lifecycle for the platform capabilities you own, from discovery and strategy through implementation, launch, adoption, and continuous improvement. • Partner with teams to understand the underlying problem, desired outcome, and value rather than simply translating requests into features. • Work with engineers and architects to translate product strategy into clear technical requirements and executable work. • Manage the product backlog, including epics, user stories, requirements, acceptance criteria, and sequencing. • Ensure teams have business and technical context to make implementation decisions. • Make prioritization and trade-off decisions across scope, value, cost, technical complexity, risk, and time to market. • Track outcomes after launch and use insights, adoption, operational data, and partner feedback to inform future investment. Platform Architecture & Capability Development • Partner with Engineering and Architecture to evolve Commerce Platform capabilities toward modular, scalable, and reusable services. • Champion API-first, domain-driven, and event-driven approaches where they create clearer boundaries and more reusable capabilities. • Help define clear contracts and interfaces between platform capabilities and their consumers. • Ensure roadmap decisions account for technical health, performance, scalability, resiliency, security, observability, and extensibility alongside new functionality. • Help guide the transition from legacy commerce capabilities to next-generation services while balancing modernization with ongoing needs. • Evaluate technology and vendor capabilities based on their ability to support the broader platform strategy rather than individual feature requirements alone. Dependency & Ecosystem Management • Lead the dependency picture for the products and capabilities you manage. • Identify upstream and downstream systems, consumers, and teams affected by product and platform changes. • Treat incomplete dependency understanding as a product risk and uncover dependencies during discovery and planning rather than during implementation. • Partner with Engineering and Architecture to reduce dependencies structurally , favoring clear contracts, stable interfaces, reusable capabilities, and asynchronous integration. • Sequence roadmap projects realistically around dependencies that remain and work with partner teams to establish commitments and shared expectations. • Ensure changes account for the broader commerce ecosystem, including product information, inventory, order management, identity, payments, fraud, pricing and promotions, search, analytics, and customer data. • Build productive relationships with the teams and partners whose systems your products consume or promote. Cross-Functional Product Leadership • Be a trusted partner to Engineering Managers, Staff and Principal Engineers, Architects, Product Managers, and partners. • Partner with customer-facing Product teams to understand their roadmaps and identify where shared Commerce Platform capabilities can ensure experiences or use cases. • Build agreement across partners when priorities, requirements, or desired solutions differ. • Provide strategic advice on how platform capabilities can address our challenges, including when the right answer is a trade-off, an alternative solution, or not building something. • Communicate product strategy, roadmap, priorities, decisions, risks, and outcomes to technical and non-technical audiences. • Represent Commerce Platform capabilities in planning and roadmap conversations with senior leaders and partner organizations. • Build relationships with external vendors and technology partners and ensure their capabilities and roadmaps align with our platform strategy. Data, Outcomes & Continuous Improvement • Define measurable outcomes and KPIs for platform investments, including adoption, reliability, performance, operational efficiency, developer experience, and growth. • Use product, operational, and engineering data to inform prioritization and investment decisions. • Measure the adoption and value of platform capabilities rather than treating technical delivery as the definition of success. • Identify opportunities to reduce friction for teams consuming Commerce Platform capabilities. • Evaluate industry trends, new technologies, and commerce platform capabilities that could influence the roadmap. • Explore opportunities to use automation and AI to improve platform capabilities, product discovery, engineering productivity, documentation, and operational processes. • Be an agent of change, challenging existing assumptions and processes when better approaches can improve customer, business, or engineering outcomes. About You • 8+ years of experience in Technical Product Management, Product Management for technical platforms, or a related role. • Experience managing product strategy and roadmaps for complex technical products or platform capabilities. • Technical fluency and demonstrated ability to participate in architecture and system design conversations. • Experience working closely with software engineers and architects on APIs, distributed systems, integrations, and modern platform architectures. • Understand complex systems, identify upstream and downstream dependencies, and reason about how product decisions affect a broader technology ecosystem. • Experience translating ambiguous business and technical problems into clear product strategies, requirements, roadmaps, and executable backlogs. • Balance customer and value with technical health, scalability, maintainability, cost, and delivery complexity. • Experience using data to support product decisions and measure outcomes. • Influence across multiple teams and organizational boundaries. • Experience communicating complex technical concepts to a variety of audiences, including the ability to explain complex technical concepts and trade-offs to senior business and technology leaders. • Comfortable bringing clarity, structure, and momentum to complex problems. • Experience building technical products or platform capabilities within digital commerce, retail, or another large-scale transactional ecosystem. • Experience with commerce platform modernization, migration, or replatforming programs. • Familiarity with commerce technologies such as SAP Commerce (Hybris), SCAYLE, or other headless or composable commerce platforms. • Experience with domain-driven design, API-first platforms, event-driven architectures, and modern integration patterns. • Familiarity with commerce domains such as product information, inventory, cart, checkout, payments, fraud, promotions, identity, search, order management, and analytics. • Experience building platforms or services consumed by multiple products, channels, markets, or engineering teams. • Experience working in global environments with distributed engineering and product teams. • Experience managing strategic relationships with technology vendors and external partners. • Experience using AI and automation to improve product management, engineering productivity, or platform operations. What Success Is A successful Lead Technical Product Manager will: • Establish a clear roadmap for the Commerce Platform capabilities they own. • Become a trusted product partner to Engineering, Architecture, Digital Product, and business leadership. • Turn recurring business and channel needs into reusable platform capabilities rather than one-off implementations. • Improve understanding between customer-facing product roadmaps and the underlying platform investments needed to promote them. • Identify dependencies and architectural constraints early and help reduce them over time. • Make technical health, scalability, reliability, and operational readiness visible product priorities. • Create clear measures of adoption and value for platform capabilities and use those measures to inform future investment. • Help evolve Commerce Platform toward clearer domain boundaries and a more modular, scalable architecture. • Help product and engineering teams to deliver new commerce experiences faster by making the underlying platform easier to understand, consume, and extend. title: Inventory & Cost Accounting Manager
jd_text: Career-defining. Life-changing. At iRhythm, you’ll have the opportunity to grow your skills and your career while impacting the lives of people around the world. iRhythm is shaping a future where everyone, everywhere can access the best possible cardiac health solutions. Every day, we collaborate, create, and constantly reimagine what’s possible. We think big and move fast, driven by our commitment to put patients first and improve lives. We need builders like you. Curious and innovative problem solvers looking for the chance to meaningfully shape the future of cardiac health, our company, and your career About This Role: iRhythm is currently seeking an experienced Inventory & Cost Accounting Manager. The responsibilities of this position will include the oversite and stewardship of the Cost Accounting processes, inclusive of ownership of inventory transactions and understanding of cost-related performance measures as it relates to cost of revenue. Additionally, this position will provide research and oversight of inventory transactions and collaborate with cross-functional teams to transition and improve processes. Our work environment is fast-paced, with a collaborative atmosphere. Most of all, we are passionate about delivering innovations that improve the quality of health care and the patient experience. We are looking for like-minded individuals to join our team today! Specific job responsibilities include: Be a subject matter expert in the manufacturing process from raw material to finished goods and cost of sales. Perform analytics throughout the month on cost of sales, absorption, PPV, and other metrics to ensure timing and accuracy of standards and gross margins. Maintain the integrity and accuracy of product cost data; assist with close activities as needed Collaborate with cross-functional teams to analyze cost accounting data and provide insights to drive business decisions. Lead matrixed team of accountants in a global organization. You will delegate process improvement projects, documentation, adhoc analysis, and support them in close by reviewing and approving month end close journal entries. Ensure compliance with the Company's policies, internal controls, procedures, and regulatory requirements (administer/maintenance of protected health information) Establish inventory policies and processes and continuously improve inventory management practices Assist cost accounting and manufacturing team in setup of manufacturing bill of materials (BOMs) and routings. Additionally, assists supply chain in material master setup of purchased parts. Identifies tasks and deliverables for implementation and assists in the creation, coordination, and execution of those tasks. In collaboration with the broader Cost Accounting/Operations FP&A team, establish KPIs and timelines as well as cadence for ongoing communications to stakeholders. Coordinate and create training for other finance, accounting, manufacturing, and procurement teams as necessary. Lead annual standards setting process – supply chain, manufacturing, and engineering update support and cost roll ups to support Annual Operating Plan (AOP). Set standard costs in ERP system. title: Sr. Specialist, IT Procurement (Software & Technology)
jd_text: Title: Sr. Specialist, IT Procurement (Software & Technology) The Sr. Specialist, IT Procurement is responsible for leading the strategic sourcing, procurement, negotiation, and supplier management of enterprise software, SaaS applications, cloud services, technology platforms, cybersecurity solutions, and other IT-related products and services. This position serves as a trusted advisor to Information Technology, Cybersecurity, Finance, Legal, Enterprise Architecture, Digital Transformation, and business stakeholders to ensure technology investments deliver maximum commercial value while minimizing financial, contractual, operational, and compliance risks. Working with limited supervision, the Sr. Specialist applies advanced procurement knowledge, commercial acumen, analytical expertise, and negotiation skills to optimize spend, improve supplier performance, support technology transformation initiatives, and ensure alignment with corporate procurement and governance requirements. The position also provides mentorship, guidance, and quality oversight to procurement specialists and junior sourcing professionals while supporting continuous improvement initiatives across the procurement organization. Key Responsibilities: Strategic Sourcing & Category Management Lead strategic sourcing and category management initiatives for enterprise software, SaaS, cloud services, cybersecurity, hardware, telecommunications, technology consulting, and related IT categories. Develop sourcing strategies aligned with business objectives and technology roadmaps; conduct market intelligence, benchmarking, supplier evaluations, and competitive RFI/RFQ/RFP processes. Evaluate supplier offerings, commercial models, and licensing structures to identify best-value solutions and cost optimization opportunities. Software & Cloud Licensing Management Negotiate software licensing, SaaS subscriptions, cloud consumption, maintenance and support renewals, and technology services agreements. jd_text: Company: INEOS Oxide Interested in joining a winning team? A team whose employees share in the ownership of the business and are empowered to make a difference? Business Context INEOS is a global manufacturer of petrochemicals and specialty chemicals, producing the raw materials that are essential in the manufacturing of a wide range of goods. The chemicals manufactured by INEOS enhance almost every aspect of modern life. INEOS is the 3rd largest petrochemical company in the world with 194 manufacturing sites across 29 countries and employing more than 26,000 people globally. INEOS Oxide is one of the most diverse, dynamic and successful businesses within INEOS, operating 4 manufacturing sites in Europe and North America. These are located at Antwerp, Belgium; Koln, Germany; Lavera, France; Plaquemine, US. INEOS Oxide is one of the world’s leading producers of Ethylene Oxide (EO) and Ethylene Oxide Derivatives (EODs), producing a broad range of 200+ products spread across 4 key value chains – Ethylene Oxide; Propylene Oxide; Oxo-alcohols & Esters; ENB. The total EO production capacity is currently > 1 million mt and the total production capacity for the overall business is ~ 3.4 million mt. Ethylene oxide (EO) is an important building block for the preparation of a wide variety of EO derivatives (EODs), including various surfactants, as well as many other chemical intermediates including Ethylene Glycols, Glycol Ethers, Polyethylene Glycols and Ethanolamine's. In 2024 INEOS Oxide acquired a new site in Bayport (TX) and the respective business in the US, which increased the total production capacity of the business to ~ 4.4 million mt and through this acquisition INEOS Oxide has achieved a true global footprint, in particular for the Ethylene Oxide value chain. Role Description The Product Manager Ethanolamine's is a key member of the INEOS Oxide US Business Team. The post holder is responsible for providing support to the Business Manager for EOAs across the full extent of the tasks involved with managing the business. Focus will be on: executing and optimizing in-month business performance to maximize EBITDA and cash delivery defining and delivering the rolling three-month business-operating plan with the Business Manager providing/maintaining databases for the annual Operating Plan maintaining a planning and modelling tool for the business that includes all input-variables to enable optimization for the business as the output Ensuring reliable product-movements to ensure optimal plant-operations/run-rates This is achieved by the Product Manager driving and coordinating a large cross-functional business team including procurement, manufacturing, supply chain, customer service and sales managers, and requires the post holder to have a deep and detailed understanding of production asset capabilities and economics, market dynamics, and customers’ service requirements and associated cost-to-serve. The Product Manager performs a key role in monitoring and responding to changing market demand for each individual product group and managing challenges arising from feedstock supply and production reliability issues. INEOS Oxide – Internal Interfaces & Factors The Product Manager will interface with, and positively influence, a large cross functional team across the INEOS Oxide business, as follows: Business Managers & Product Managers – EO swap, EOA sales in Europe, EOA arbitrage, optimizing margins on a global basis together with Lavera EOA volumes. Raw Material Procurement Team – agreeing and executing raw material procurement objectives. Plaquemine Site Operations – monitoring manufacturing performance; managing product supply. Logistics & Supply Chain Teams – agreeing and executing drumming, storage, and transportation requirements. Sales & Customer Service Teams – agreeing and executing the sales and contracting strategies for the business. INEOS Oxide Back-Office Support Functions – dealing with cross business and commercial process issues. Manage day-to-day and mid-term production, sales and margin planning and optimize sales/production variations. Maintain Dashboard and cost/price/margin data to aid in development of long-term plans and presentations. External Interfaces & Factors Executing this role effectively will require a wide-ranging engagement with parties in the external market: Suppliers – supporting the Procurement Team in key raw material supply negotiations. Customers – supporting the Sales Team in key contract preparations and potentially negotiations. Manage Customer relationship and business with 1 critically important customer and possibly up to 3 customers that can have significant impact on the EOA-plant operations Co-producers – supporting the business managers to pursue swap, toll and strategic partnership opportunities. Publications – discussions with publications, supporting Business Manager, to discuss market news and to inform them of INEOS specific information, as appropriate. INEOS O&P US – dealing with Ethylene market information. Legal – work on resolving contract and other challenges that require input from counsel. Technical Service – coordinate Product Data/Specification/Safety Information handling and changes. Accountabilities Accountability 1 - Business Operating Plan Execution Develop and maintain the rolling 3 month operational and financial forecast in line with supply/demand balances and product pricing policy and agree them with the Business Manager prior to his submission of the plan to the company’s formal financial forecasting process. Together with the planner, define and optimize production plan based on demand, inventory and raw material availability, to maximize business EBITDA and cash generation. Monitor and manage supply-demand balances to ensure availability of product for sale, and to ensure EBITDA, cash and working capital targets are met. Implement agreed inventory management strategy to achieve defined stock targets. It translates finance and operations problems — forecasting, reporting, reconciliation, transfer pricing, deal support, backlog analytics — into solution designs that are scalable, secure, governable and supportable, and it holds the line on architecture standards when delivery pressure argues otherwise. It is an advanced role, but not a detached one. The architect is expected to write code when a pattern needs proving, run the proof of concept personally, and lead engineers and vendor teams through the build rather than handing over a deck and stepping away. Architecture Ownership Own the target-state architecture for AI, GenAI, agentic AI and automation solutions across the Finance Transformation portfolio, and maintain the roadmap that moves the estate towards it. Produce solution architecture artefacts to enterprise standard: context and component diagrams, integration and data-flow designs, sequence flows, non-functional requirements, and documented architecture decision records with the options considered and the rationale for the choice. Make and defend build-versus-buy, platform-selection and pattern decisions, stating explicitly the trade-offs in cost, delivery time, supportability and risk. Define reusable reference architectures, solution patterns and shared components so that each new use case starts from an established baseline rather than a blank page. Own non-functional design across performance, scalability, availability, cost, observability and supportability, and set the acceptance thresholds each solution must meet before production. Run design reviews and technical governance forums, and take solutions through enterprise architecture review, security review and data governance approval. Maintain a current view of the solution landscape — what exists, what it depends on, what is being retired — and prevent duplicate or divergent builds across teams. AI and Agentic Solution Design Architect LLM and agentic solutions end to end: orchestration and agent topology, tool and function calling, retrieval and grounding strategy, memory and state, human-in-the-loop checkpoints, and fallback behaviour when the model is wrong. Design retrieval-augmented generation over enterprise content, including chunking and embedding strategy, index design, source-of-truth selection, freshness and permission-trimmed retrieval. Define the evaluation and assurance approach for AI solutions: golden datasets, accuracy and groundedness measures, regression testing on prompt or model change, and the criteria that decide whether a solution is fit to go live. Design guardrails and responsible-AI controls covering prompt injection, data leakage, hallucination containment, PII handling, auditability of AI-assisted decisions, and the boundary between what the agent decides and what a person approves. Set the model strategy — model selection, routing, versioning, cost and token management, and the approach to upgrades — and revisit it as the platform landscape moves. Determine where machine learning, deterministic automation, or a conventional application is the right answer, and say so plainly when generative AI is not the appropriate tool for the problem. Data and Platform Architecture Design the data architecture underpinning AI and analytics use cases: source systems, ingestion patterns, curated layers, semantic models, lineage and refresh cadence. Architect solutions on Microsoft Azure, Greenlake and Databricks, selecting the appropriate compute, storage, orchestration and serving components for each workload. Design integration architecture across enterprise platforms such as SAP, Salesforce, Anaplan, ServiceNow and Power BI, covering API, event and batch patterns, error handling, idempotency and reconciliation between systems. Define identity, access and secrets architecture using Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, OAuth, managed identities and role-based access control, and ensure least-privilege design is applied rather than assumed. Set the deployment architecture across environments, including CI/CD approach, promotion path, environment parity, configuration management and rollback strategy. Design for control and audit readiness where solutions touch financial data, including SOX-aligned controls, evidence capture, segregation of duties and traceability from output back to source. Delivery Leadership Lead engineers, data teams and vendor partners through implementation, reviewing designs and code against the agreed architecture and correcting drift early. Build proofs of concept personally to de-risk unproven patterns, and convert what is learned into a documented pattern the team can reuse. Break large initiatives into deliverable increments with clear technical dependencies, sequencing and defensible estimates. Identify architectural risk, technical debt and single points of failure early, quantify the impact, and put a remediation path in front of decision-makers before it becomes an incident. Support production stabilisation after release, lead root-cause analysis on significant technical failures, and feed the findings back into the architecture. Raise the technical capability of the team through design mentoring, code and design review, internal enablement sessions and written guidance. Stakeholder and Governance Engagement Work directly with Finance, Operations and Transformation leadership to understand the business problem behind the request, and challenge the requirement where the stated ask will not deliver the intended outcome. Present architecture, options, cost implications and risk positions to senior business and technology stakeholders, adjusting depth to the audience without diluting the substance. title: Senior Manager, Oracle EPM Platforms
jd_text: Position Summary We are seeking a hands-on Senior Manager to serve as the architect and platform owner for our Oracle Enterprise Performance Management (EPM) Cloud landscape, spanning EPBCS (Planning & Budgeting), FCCS (Financial Consolidation), ARCS (Account Reconciliation) and EDMCS (Enterprise Data Management). This role owns the end-to-end architecture, integration design, and roadmap across all four platforms, and acts as the primary escalation point our internal teams & vendors. The role is expected to lead concurrent EPM implementation and enhancement projects. The ideal candidate is equally comfortable writing calculation manager scripts and Groovy business rules as they are setting strategy with finance and IT leadership — someone who can design, build, and troubleshoot personally, while directing and holding both a managed service team and parallel implementation teams accountable to timelines, quality, and roadmap commitments. Key Responsibilities Architecture & Platform Ownership • Own the end-to-end solution architecture across EPBCS, FCCS, ARCS, and EDMCS, ensuring designs are scalable, secure, and aligned to enterprise data and finance standards. • Design and build EPM Cloud configurations (Essbase/hybrid, business rules, calculation manager scripts, Groovy business rules, task lists, forms, and dashboards) directly, without relying solely on the managed service team for build work. • Architect and maintain integrations between EDMCS and downstream applications (EPBCS, FCCS, ARCS) to ensure consistent dimensionality, mappings, and hierarchy governance across the metadata model. • Design and support data integration pipelines (EPM Automate, REST APIs, Data Management/FDMEE, Data Integration) between EPM applications, the GL/ERP source systems, and downstream reporting tools. • Configure and optimize reconciliation rules, matching logic, and workflows for account reconciliations in ARCS, aligned with close calendar and controls requirements. Key Responsibilities • Define and maintain the multi-year technology roadmap for the EPM platform footprint, incorporating Oracle's quarterly cloud release features, new capabilities, and deprecations. • Direct and coordinate EPM support team, acting as the primary point of contact for day-to-day operations, incident escalation, enhancement requests, and release coordination. • Review and validate MSP deliverables (SLAs, response/resolution times, ticket quality, code/config standards) against contractual and internal expectations, and drive corrective action when performance slips. • Author technical specifications and architecture guardrails for tasks assigned to the managed service team, including detailed requirements, test plans, and acceptance criteria, to ensure work is built correctly the first time. • Serve as the technical liaison between the MSP and internal stakeholders, translating business requirements into technical scope the service team can execute against. • Manage the shared backlog of enhancements, defects, and change requests across all four platforms, prioritizing based on business impact, risk, and platform roadmap. Stakeholder & Team Leadership • Partner directly with FP&A, Accounting/Controllership, and Financial Reporting leadership to translate evolving business requirements into platform enhancements. • Present regularly on architecture decisions, platform health, roadmap progress, and risk to finance and IT executive leadership. • Maintain deep functional knowledge of the underlying business processes (planning, consolidation, reconciliation, and master data management) to design fit-for-purpose solutions rather than one-off fixes. • Mentor or oversee a small internal team of EPM analysts/administrators where applicable, in addition to managing the external managed service relationship. Platform Scope Direct architectural and functional ownership across the following Oracle EPM Cloud modules: • EPBCS (Enterprise Planning & Budgeting Cloud Service): Multi-dimensional planning, budgeting, and forecasting models; Smart View/Web forms; business rules; workforce, capital, and project planning modules as applicable. • FCCS (Financial Consolidation & Close Cloud Service): Financial consolidation, intercompany eliminations, currency translation, ownership management, and close process automation. • ARCS (Account Reconciliation Cloud Service): Reconciliation compliance, transaction matching, integration with source sub-ledgers, and close task automation. • EDMCS (Enterprise Data Management Cloud Service): Enterprise dimension and hierarchy governance, metadata synchronization, and mapping across all connected EPM and ERP applications. Required Qualifications • 8+ years of progressive experience in Finance Systems, IT, or Enterprise Applications, with at least 4+ years in a hands-on Oracle EPM architect or lead role. • Demonstrated hands-on experience building configuring, and supporting at least three of the four platforms: EPBCS, FCCS, ARCS, EDMCS. • Prior experience managing a managed service provider (MSP) or managing outsourced/offshore application support teams against SLAs. • Proven track record running multiple concurrent EPM implementation projects (e.g., new module rollouts, upgrades, migrations) alongside steady-state managed services, including coordinating systems integrators or contract resources across overlapping timelines. • Strong working knowledge with EPM Automate, REST/SOAP APIs, Groovy (business rule scripting), Data Management/FDMEE, and Smart View. • Solid understanding of Essbase concepts (block storage/aggregate storage), dimension design, and calculation logic. • Working knowledge of core FP&A, consolidation, and account reconciliation business processes and controls (e.g., SOX). • Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to communicate technical concepts to finance executives. • Bachelor's degree in Business Administration, Finance, Accounting, Information Systems, or a related field (or equivalent experience). Preferred Qualifications • Oracle EPM Cloud certification(s) (e.g., Oracle EPM Cloud implementation certifications for Planning, FCCS, ARCS, or EDMCS). • Prior experience in a multi-entity, multi-currency organization supporting a large or global enterprise environment. • Experience integrating EPM Cloud (e.g., through Data Integration/FDMEE) to major ERP platforms (Oracle Fusion, SAP, Workday, NetSuite, etc.). • SQL or scripting experience (PowerShell, Python, VBScript, or similar) for automation of EPM operational tasks. • Familiarity of Oracle's quarterly readiness process and change management practices for cloud EPM environments. Key Competencies • Hands-on technical depth. Able to write scripts, calc rules, and integrations personally, not only review others' work. • Systems thinking. Sees the platform landscape as one connected ecosystem rather than four siloed tools. • Vendor/service management. Comfortable directing a third-party team's day-to-day work while owning ultimate accountability for outcomes. • Judgment under pressure. Drives issues to resolution and proactively identifies risks before they affect the close or planning cycle. • Parallel workstream management. title: Procurement Process Manager
jd_text: About the Role Integrity's Procure-to-Pay (P2P) function is a critical enabler of operational efficiency, financial control, and scalable growth. Our P2P organization is focused on delivering standardized, connected, and optimized processes across procurement and payables while driving a culture of continuous improvement and operational excellence. As a Procurement Process Manager, you will play a key role in ensuring all components of the Procure-to-Pay lifecycle are fully integrated, aligned, and operating efficiently. This role has a strong emphasis on operations, execution discipline, and driving efficiency across the end-to-end P2P process. You will act as a process leader and change agent, ensuring that P2P operations are streamlined, scalable, compliant, and well understood across the organization. Success in this role will depend heavily on strong stakeholder management, enabling alignment, adoption, and accountability across diverse business partners. The ideal candidate will bring deep understanding of end-to-end P2P operations and the ability to enhance performance through process discipline, data insights, and stakeholder engagement. This role requires someone who can translate operational challenges into actionable improvements, proactively identify gaps (including off-channel spend), and partner effectively across teams to drive adoption and compliance. The ideal candidate will have a demonstrated ability to identify and capture value from supplier relationships—going beyond cost savings to uncover opportunities for service improvements, innovation, and strategic partnership. They should be comfortable leveraging supplier data and performance metrics to surface actionable insights that benefit the organization. Strong stakeholder management is critical—this individual must be able to influence, communicate, and build trust across all levels of the organization while driving alignment and results. The successful candidate will be a proactive problem solver with a continuous improvement mindset, strong operational rigor, and a focus on delivering measurable efficiency gains. Key Responsibilities Operational Excellence & Process Efficiency Drive efficiency and effectiveness across all Procure-to-Pay operations. Ensure seamless integration and connectivity across requisitioning, purchasing, invoicing, and payment processes. Establish and reinforce standardized processes and best practices. Stakeholder Management & Engagement Build and maintain strong relationships with Procurement, AP, Finance, and business stakeholders. Act as a trusted partner and primary point of contact for P2P operational topics. Drive alignment, accountability, and adoption of P2P processes across the organization. Lead stakeholder communication, ensuring clarity and consistency. Training & Educational Activities Develop and deliver training programs to improve user adoption and compliance. Continuously reinforce process adherence through education and engagement Supplier Value Management Identify and capture value from supplier relationships beyond cost—including service quality, innovation, risk mitigation, and strategic partnership opportunities. Develop and maintain supplier scorecards and performance frameworks to drive accountability and continuous improvement. Collaborate with category managers and business owners to maximize the value delivered through supplier engagements. Off-Channel Spend Management Identify, analyze, and address off-contract and off-channel spend. Partner with stakeholders to drive compliance with approved procurement channels. Recommend and implement strategies to improve spend control and visibility. Performance Management (KPIs & Scorecards) Monitor, and report key operational KPIs. Develop and maintain stakeholder and operational scorecards. Design and deliver proactive reporting that surfaces trends, risks, and opportunities before they escalate—enabling leadership to make informed decisions with timely, forward-looking insights. Use data to identify trends, measure performance, and drive continuous improvement. Governance & Compliance Support development and enforcement of procurement policies and controls. Ensure adherence to financial, regulatory, and internal compliance requirements. Assist with audits and ensure proper documentation and process transparency. Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Supply Chain, Accounting, or related field (or equivalent experience). 5+ years of experience in Procure-to-Pay, Procurement Operations, or Finance Operations. Strong understanding of end-to-end P2P processes and operational workflows. Proven track record of improving operational efficiency and process performance. Demonstrated ability to identify and realize value from supplier relationships across cost, quality, and innovation dimensions. Experience designing and delivering proactive reporting and actionable insights to senior stakeholders. Strong stakeholder management and influencing skills across all organizational levels. Excellent communication and interpersonal skills. Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities. Experience identifying and addressing off-channel spend is highly preferred. Familiarity with procurement and financial systems (e.g., Coupa, SAP, Ariba, or similar) is a plus. What You’ll Work On In this role, you will collaborate closely with Procurement, Finance, and business teams to deliver a highly efficient, connected, and scalable Procure-to-Pay operation.
